cases.name: built-in worked example
stdout: === A. THE ANNOUNCEMENT (what most founders send) ===
A clear reason for now · 30/110 (27%) · Do not pitch yet
Blocked on: Survives the company-removed test; Passes the forward-to-a-colleague test; Method is written down. These are the checks a journalist applies in the first ten seconds.
- Survives the company-removed test — Strip your company name out. If nothing is left, there was never a story
- Passes the forward-to-a-colleague test — A reader forwarding it is the only readership signal you control before publication
- Method is written down — A figure whose method you cannot show is a figure you should not pitch
- Someone else could reproduce it — Reproducibility is what makes a data story citable rather than quotable
- Already published on your own site — Journalists prefer data that has a home, a method and a chart (Step 4)
- Audience named — Step 1: 'We want [audience] to see us in [outlet] so that [outcome]'
- At least three named outlets that reach them — 1 named — twenty of the right names beats two thousand of the wrong ones
materials not ready: Current headshots; Written method behind any data you share
=== B. THE SAME QUARTER, REWORKED AS A STORY ===
"Mid-market HR teams are rebuilding onboarding around the first 30 days"
The story stands without your company name, the evidence holds, and the list is aimed.
One follow-up after a few days, with something new. Then stop.
This is a rubric, not a prediction. No score here makes coverage likely.
Paid placement is advertising even when it looks like an article.
